From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material point. Several items are labelled [STANDARD] or "FINAL, not to be re-opened," and the reviewer note asks us to skip anything not marked [OPEN]. We should not accept that. The labels don't change our positions. Several of the clauses marked [STANDARD] are the ones that most depart from the playbook. Nothing in the file shows that Amelia Frost gave the written authority the playbook requires for any of the Seller's fallback positions, so we should not treat any of these terms as agreed.

I've worked from the Seller's summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA text. Each clause needs checking against the actual drafting by NSW counsel before we send a mark-up.

## 1. Departures and recommended pushback

### A. Critical: structural risks

**1. Title and capacity placed under the general regime (Seller "Fundamental/Title" proposal)**
- *Seller:* Title and capacity warranties subject to the general cap, time limit and basket "for administrative simplicity."
- *Playbook:* Separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- *Why it matters:* This is the core protection for a 100% share purchase. Putting it under the general regime would cap it at AUD 4.8M and cut it off at 18 months.
- *Push back:* Reject outright. Restore the separate Fundamental regime, with no basket, de minimis or buyer-knowledge bar applying.

**2. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and DL 1.1 / 1.2)**
- *Seller:* The whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 and everything referred to in it), public registers, statutory registers and the Accounts are disclosed generally.
- *Playbook:* Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- *Why it matters:* Read literally, almost every fact we have diligenced is disclosed against every warranty. This combined with the buyer-knowledge clause (item 4) would leave the warranties close to empty for anything in the data room.
- *Push back:* Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Require disclosure against specific warranties, identified with reasonable particularity.

**3. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)**
- *Seller:* No Buyer claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records.
- *Playbook:* Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and a reasonable-enquiry standard. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- *Push back:* Delete clause 8.3. If the Seller insists on a knowledge qualifier, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and carve out title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

**4. Fraud carve-out missing (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)**
- *Seller:* Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- *Playbook:* Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- *Push back:* Insert the carve-out, with a non-waiver provision. Its absence is a serious gap, and it should be treated as a condition of any further discussion.

### B. High: economic terms

**5. General cap (Clause 12.1)**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4.8M.
- *Playbook:* Starting position 25% / AUD 6.0M. The 20% / AUD 4.8M fallback is available only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given.
- *Push back:* Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0M. Do not offer the fallback without written authority.

**6. Thresholds (Clause 12.2)**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable.
- *Playbook:* De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, then first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- *Why it matters:* The Seller's basket is about 1.04% of price. Ours is about 0.21%. On a loss of AUD 300,000, we would recover AUD 300,000 under our terms and only AUD 50,000 under theirs, a AUD 250,000 gap.
- *Push back:* Restore AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket, and first-dollar recovery. The "around 1% of price" market claim is not our playbook and does not justify conceding.

**7. General claims period (Clauses 12.3 / 13)**
- *Seller:* 18 months. Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims.
- *Playbook:* 24 months. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "all Claims" wording is a hidden general-regime override, which the playbook prohibits.
- *Push back:* Counter at 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" wording so each category keeps its own period.

**8. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3; DL 2)**
- *Seller:* Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- *Playbook:* Require effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- *Facts:* Bluefen is about AUD 3.6M of FY26 revenue (~30%). DL 2 confirms that no final written consent is included and that conditions under clause 11.3 have not been evidenced.
- *Push back:* Make effective consent, plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, a condition precedent to Completion. Include a walk-right and a price mechanism if it is not met.

**9. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2 / 7; DL 3)**
- *Seller:* About AUD 3.2M outstanding, to be released "following Completion."
- *Playbook:* Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- *Facts:* The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is in the file.
- *Push back:* Require a current payout letter. Repay Riverlark directly from Completion funds, treated as debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics. Require security releases at Completion. Do not accept a post-completion release.

**10. Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DL 5)**
- *Seller:* AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- *Playbook:* The AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- *Push back:* Require either an itemised deduction from the price or a specific Seller-funded indemnity, covering the bonuses and all payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. Require the Seller to quantify on-costs. Confirm the treatment in the funds flow itself.

### C. Medium: specific issues

**11. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1; DL 4)**
- *Seller:* The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- *Playbook:* Broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- *Facts:* Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- *Push back:* Broaden the indemnity to cover ownership and transfer defects in the IP generally. Keep the SOW3 cure mechanism. Require a confirmatory assignment and evidence of payment status, such as a supplier confirmation or bank records. Do not treat AUD 180,000 as confirmed either way.

**12. Export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; DL 6)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- *Playbook:* Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- *Facts:* A download link went to an unintended external address. The file may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification are all undetermined.
- *Push back:* Do not accept the Seller's materiality characterisation as a basis for limiting any warranty. Require preservation of logs, a written investigation plan with a timeline, and regular written updates. Note that the Seller's clause references (4.6 and Schedule 6) do not match the disclosure letter's section 6, which should be corrected. Whether a specific indemnity is needed is a deal-team judgement and is not set by the playbook.

**13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DL 8)**
- *Seller:* Ordinary-course operating costs.
- *Playbook:* Assess them. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- *Facts:* DD-008 and DD-011 record three renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- *Push back:* Do not accept the ordinary-course label without evidence. Request the contracts, terms and timing. Confirm that DD-008 and DD-011 are not describing the same renewals twice. Assess them before deciding whether any treatment is needed. Do not make an automatic price adjustment.

**14. Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)**
- *Facts:* The lease has a notification obligation, and the Mossvale agreement has an assignment restriction. Neither disclosure states whether consent is required for the share sale.
- *Playbook:* Not addressed directly. These are open diligence items.
- *Push back:* Request counsel's analysis of both documents, including whether the share sale triggers any consent or change-of-control provision. If consent is needed, treat it as a condition precedent.

**15. Title evidence (DL 10; Seller title statement)**
- *Seller:* Title is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012.
- *Playbook:* Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- *Push back:* Reject the DD-012 reliance. Require an ASIC company extract, a PPSR search over the shares, executed share transfer forms, confirmation that the shares are free of encumbrances, and evidence of the Seller's authority and capacity.

### D. Open: Tax and IP

**16. Tax and IP positions**
- *Seller:* Considered "settled under the general regime."
- *Playbook:* Remain OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Keep them separate from the general regime.
- *Push back:* Reject the "settled" characterisation. Keep these categories open and separate in the mark-up.

## 2. Process points

- **Labels and efficiency note.** The [STANDARD] and FINAL markings don't bind us. Several clauses so marked are the most significant departures. We should review the whole package.
- **"Agreed at principal level."** We have no record of Amelia Frost agreeing any of these positions. Before treating anything as agreed, we should confirm this with her.
- **"Market" claims.** The Seller's market assertions do not change our playbook positions.
- **Data room cut-off.** The data room is indexed as at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Disclosures, including the DD-006 status and the Riverlark and Bluefen positions, may be stale. We should require a refreshed data room and disclosure letter.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Must-have before any further negotiation:**
1. Restore the separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
2. Insert the fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out, non-waivable.
3. Delete the whole-data-room, public-register and accounts deemed disclosure. Require specific disclosure.
4. Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (clause 8.3).
5. Make effective Bluefen consent, with evidence that its conditions are satisfied, a condition precedent to Completion. Remove consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours language.
6. Riverlark: current payout, repayment from Completion funds, and security releases at Completion.
7. Bonuses: itemise the AUD 420,000 and on-costs in the funds flow, or make them seller-funded with an indemnity.

**Economic counter-offers:**
8. General cap: 25% / AUD 6.0M. Do not offer the 20% fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority.
9. De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded.
10. General claims period 24 months. Do not offer 18 months without written approval. Delete the "applies to all Claims" wording.

**Specific issues:**
11. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and require a confirmatory assignment and evidence of payment status.
12. DD-006: preservation, investigation plan and regular updates. No materiality concession. Assume no confirmed breach or numeric demand.
13. Sandbar: request contracts and assess. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
14. Lease and Mossvale: obtain legal analysis on consent. Treat any required consent as a condition precedent.
15. Title: independent evidence (ASIC extract, PPSR search, transfer forms, authority). Reject DD-012 as proof.
16. Tax and IP: keep open and separate.

**Process:**
17. Review the full SPA text, not only the summary.
18. Confirm with Amelia Frost that none of the Seller's positions has been agreed.
19. Request a refreshed data room and disclosure letter.
